messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — SEV: P1. High error rate observed on model deployment 'open-redwood-13b-canary' serving in eu-central-1. Alert: 5xx spikes and p95 latency regressions. Page routed to: @anika (oncall).

anika (oncall): I see alerts. Acknowledge. Starting triage. Does this affect hosted or dedicated customers?

ben (support): Support signals: two small customers reported degraded generation and timeouts in the last 8 minutes (ticket 3821, 3822). No broad CS rush yet.

matt (eng-sre): Looking at metrics — canary traffic = 7% of EU fleet. Error rate jumped from 0.2% -> 4.8% at 10:41 UTC. p95 latency from ~120ms -> ~520ms. Logs incoming.

sofia (ml-release): Canary was a rollout of model v2026-03-12-quant-lite (no architecture change). Only changed tokenization fallback. Rolling back w/o approval is heavy; collect diffs.

anika (oncall): Share recent logs and rollout config. Also check if pinning was in place for Dedicated customers.

matt (eng-sre): kubectl logs snippets:
```
2026-03-15T10:40:52Z ERROR kv_cache.cpp: failed to retrieve KV for seq=1024 size=128 -> timeout
2026-03-15T10:41:01Z WARN runtime.cpp: decode_batch failed (op=lm_infer) err=INVALID_ARG
2026-03-15T10:41:05Z ERROR http.cpp: 502 downstream timeout serving request id=... 
```

matt (eng-sre): Hypothesis 1: new quantized kernels introduced a decode regression under longer contexts leading to retries/timeouts. Hypothesis 2: memory pressure causing KV cache thrash.

sofia (ml-release): I ran a quick canary-diff vs baseline v2026-02-28-stable: tokenization change added fallback path for rare unicode. Diff: small change in tokenizer.py and a new kernel flag use_fast_decode=false by default. No other runtime code.

anika (oncall): Can we toggle kernel flag remotely or pin model to previous artifact for canary only?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout id=cr-2026-03-12-47. Current traffic distribution: stable=93%, canary=7%. Rollback command: /rollout rollback cr-2026-03-12-47 --target canary

matt (eng-sre): I'm testing a quick patch: set use_fast_decode=true on canary hosts, will flip for eu region. Running a curl to health endpoint:
```
curl -i https://eu-host-1.internal/health
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"uptime": "2d", "queued": 3}
```

anika (oncall): If flipping doesn't stabilize within 5m we rollback the canary. ben, prep customer comms saying we're investigating model rollout and may rollback.

ben (support): Acknowledged — drafting: "We are aware of degraded generation for a subset of EU requests. Engineers are validating a canary rollback; we'll update within 15 minutes."

sofia (ml-release): I verified that Dedicated customers with version pinning remain on v2026-02-28-stable — no impact there. Confirmed via config query.

matt (eng-sre): After toggling use_fast_decode=true on canary hosts, error rate dropped to 0.5% and p95 back to ~140ms at 10:48 UTC. Logs show fewer decode failures.

anika (oncall): Good. Keep monitoring for 30m. No rollback required. Action items:
- sofia: open a PR to revert risky quant flag and add gating tests. (done)
- matt: run a retrospective on KV cache patterns and add alert for decode failures.
- ben: follow up with affected customers and close tickets after stabilization.

sofia (ml-release): PR opened: https://git.redwood/s/PR-#4782 — adds an integration test targeting the unicode fallback path + perf assertions. Tagging @matt for review.

matt (eng-sre): I'll review. Also adding an incident timeline entry to the oncall handoff doc.

deploy-bot: Incident annotated: incident-id=inc-2026-0315-89, severity=P1, status=mitigated. Remember to run RCA workflow and link logs: s3://redwood-logs/inc-2026-0315-89/*

anika (oncall): Handoff to morning oncall @mika at 11:15 UTC. I'll include steps taken and watchlist. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

mika: acknowledged, will take over monitoring and follow RCA.
